items.title: 4.2 Relationship between mole, molar mass and Avogadro's number (in ka aapas mein talluq) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 4.2, printed pages 76-78, with the sample problems worked and Quick Check 4.2 answered.

blocks.text: 12.0 g natural (qudrati) carbon mein utne hi atoms hain jitne 4.0 g qudrati helium mein. Dono mein atoms ka 1 mole hai, yani 6.02 x 10²³ atoms.
Dilchasp baat yeh hai ke alag alag elements ke alag alag masses mein atoms ki tadaad ek jaisi ho sakti hai:

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}1.0\ \text{g of hydrogen} &= 1\ \text{mol of hydrogen} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{atoms of H}\\ 23.0\ \text{g of sodium} &= 1\ \text{mol of Na} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{atoms of Na}\\ 238.0\ \text{g of uranium} &= 1\ \text{mol of U} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{atoms of U}\end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: 1.0 g of hydrogen = 1 mol of hydrogen = 6.02 x 10²³ atoms of H; 23.0 g of sodium = 1 mol of Na = 6.02 x 10²³ atoms of Na; 238.0 g of uranium = 1 mol of U = 6.02 x 10²³ atoms of U

blocks.text: Sodium ka ek atom hydrogen ke ek atom se 23 guna bhaari hai. Is liye barabar atoms lene hon to sodium ka mass hydrogen se 23 guna zyada lena hoga.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}18.0\ \text{g of }\ce{H2O} &= 1\ \text{mol of water} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{molecules of water}\\ 180.0\ \text{g of glucose} &= 1\ \text{mol of glucose} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{molecules of glucose}\end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: 18.0 g of H₂O = 1 mol of water = 6.02 x 10²³ molecules of water; 180.0 g of glucose = 1 mol of glucose = 6.02 x 10²³ molecules of glucose

blocks.text: Yani alag alag compounds ke ek mole ka mass alag alag hota hai, lekin molecules ki tadaad ek jaisi hoti hai.
Isi tarah alag alag ions ke ek mole mein ions ki tadaad bhi hamesha Avogadro’s number hoti hai:

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}96.1\ \text{g of }\ce{SO4^2-} &= 1\ \text{mole of }\ce{SO4^2-} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{ions of }\ce{SO4^2-}\\ 62.0\ \text{g of }\ce{NO3^{1-}} &= 1\ \text{mole of }\ce{NO3^{1-}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{ions of }\ce{NO3^{1-}}\end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: 96.1 g of SO₄²⁻ = 1 mole of SO₄²⁻ = 6.02 x 10²³ ions of SO₄²⁻; 62.0 g of NO₃¹⁻ = 1 mole of NO₃¹⁻ = 6.02 x 10²³ ions of NO₃¹⁻

blocks.text: Particles ki tadaad ko Avogadro’s number se divide karein to moles mil jate hain:

blocks.latex: \text{Number of moles} = \frac{\text{No. of particles of a substance}}{\text{Avogadro's Number}}
blocks.text_alt: Number of moles = No. of particles of a substance / Avogadro’s Number

blocks.text: Moles aur particles (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons) ka relationship (talluq) yeh hai:

blocks.latex: \text{Number of particles} = \frac{\text{Mass of substance} \times N_A}{\text{Molar Mass}}
blocks.text_alt: Number of particles = Mass of substance x Nₐ / Molar Mass

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke is formula mein “subtance” chhapa hai; sahi lafz “substance” hai.

blocks.alt: Ek line mein teen dark blue boxes: baen taraf 'Mass in grams', beech mein 'Moles' aur daen taraf 'No. of Particles'. Ek grey arrow Moles se Mass in grams ki taraf hai, us par 'x Molar mass' likha hai. Doosra grey arrow Moles se No. of Particles ki taraf hai, us par 'x Avogadro's number' likha hai.
blocks.caption: Grams mein mass, moles aur particles ki tadaad (kitab ke page 77 par chhapi scheme ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Moles beech mein hain. Moles ko molar mass se multiply karein to grams mein mass milta hai; moles ko Avogadro’s number (6.02 x 10²³) se multiply karein to particles ki tadaad milti hai. Ulta jaana ho to divide karein: mass ÷ molar mass = moles, aur particles ÷ 6.02 x 10²³ = moles.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke is diagram (khaka) mein baen taraf ka label “Molar x mass” chhapa hai. Matlab “x Molar mass” hai: moles ko molar mass se multiply karein to mass milta hai, bilkul daen taraf ke “x Avogadro’s number” ki tarah. Oopar diagram mein yahi likha gaya hai.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.4
blocks.problem: Glucose ke ek sample mein 3.76 x 10²⁴ molecules hain. Is mein kitne moles hain?
steps: Moles = molecules ki tadaad ÷ Avogadro’s number

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.5
blocks.problem: 2.3 g sodium metal mein kitne atoms hain?
steps: Atoms = moles x Nₐ = 0.1 x 6.02 x 10²³

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.6
blocks.problem: Juglone ek dye (rang) hai jo kale akhrot (black walnut) ke chhilkon se banti hai. Is ka formula C₁₀H₆O₃ hai. a) Juglone ka molar mass nikalein. b) 0.87 g juglone mein kitne moles hain?
steps: a) Molar mass = 10 × Aᵣ(C) + 6 × Aᵣ(H) + 3 × Aᵣ(O)
b) Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 0.87 g ÷ 174 g mol⁻¹

blocks.title: Interesting Information! (dilchasp baat)
blocks.text: Juglone ek natural herbicide (ghaas-phoos maarne wali dawa) hai. Yeh akhrot ke darakht ke gird competitive (muqabla karne wale) paudon ko maar deti hai, magar ghaas aur doosre paudon ko nuqsan nahi deti.

blocks.prompt: a) Tanbe (copper) ki ek taar mein 27.10 × 10²⁵ copper atoms hain. Copper ke moles nikalein.
b) Shehad ki makhi ke dank mein nikalne wale 1 x 10⁻⁶ g isopentyl acetate, C₇H₁₄O₂, mein kitne molecules hain? Us mein carbon, hydrogen aur oxygen ke kitne atoms hain?
blocks.explanation: Molar mass = 7 x 12 + 14 x 1 + 2 x 16 = 130 g/mol. Moles = 1 x 10⁻⁶ ÷ 130 = 7.7 x 10⁻⁹ mol. Molecules = 7.7 x 10⁻⁹ x 6.02 x 10²³ = 4.6 x 10¹⁵. Har molecule mein 7 C, 14 H aur 2 O hain: carbon atoms 3.2 x 10¹⁶, hydrogen atoms 6.5 x 10¹⁶, oxygen atoms 9.3 x 10¹⁵.

blocks.title: Interesting Information! (dilchasp baat)
blocks.text: Isopentyl acetate (C₇H₁₄O₂) kelon (bananas) ki khushbu ki wajah hai. Shehad ki makhi dank maarte waqt is ka taqreeban 1 μg (1 × 10⁻⁶ g) chhorti hai. Yeh khushbu doosri makhiyon ko attack (hamla) ke liye bula leti hai.

items: Har substance ke 1 mole mein 6.02 x 10²³ particles hote hain, mass chahe kuch bhi ho: 1.0 g H, 23.0 g Na, 18.0 g H₂O, 96.1 g SO₄²⁻.
Moles = particles ÷ Nₐ; particles = mass x Nₐ ÷ molar mass.
